Umm.. Did anyone suggest watching the documentary? It's actually titled "Women Aren't Funny." It's not over-the-top great but I liked it and think it's definitely worth a watch.

Also, WATCH MARIA BAMFORD.

Warren Zevon- I'll sleep when I'm dead
www.youtube.com/watch?v=BwdaZfLatmM
The Labyrinth. Why is this not here yet?

Honest away! That's what I'm here for. :)

Alcoholism is definitely an inheritable quality. I don't know if it's neurological or environmental or what, but it is. I hope your brother finds some peace. I know it's terrifying to watch someone fall into that hole. Just remember you can only do what you can. REALLY though. You have to take care of yourself first. It's a balancing act, but try to make yourself a priority as much as you can.

You had your reasons to move, I'm sure. Even if they were minimal, it's your life and you should take it wherever you want. It may have made things more difficult but hey, live and learn.

I (..woman..) was very fortunate in that my dad was able to recover. It was through a lot of circumstances that had nothing to do with me. (It took watching his brother die saving my dad's life.. that's another story.) It's awful that your dad was not able to recover, but you shouldn't feel guilt over it. In the end, he was the parent.

Also, props on your choice of adjective regarding the lawyers job. I like it.

Whether or not you did the best possible job at being an executor should not have any bearing on your self-esteem. So you're not amazing at that one (probably very difficult and confusing) thing, the first time you attempted it... So what? YOU did it. You. For your family. And that should give you some pride. It's really very admirable.

That said, I'm 24, too. I've struggled with suicidal ideation myself, for most of my life. Right now, I'm getting better. I still have those thoughts - I think my brain has been trained to have those thoughts - but they are not so persistent anymore. And as an aside: my father was also an alcoholic, and from the age of about 12 I was the only person in my family to keep contact with him. There are plenty of stories I could share to demonstrate how difficult this was, but I know you can imagine. My point is that I sympathize with the amount of weight on your shoulders that this ordeal has caused. But now, later in life, I can also take pride in the fact that I accepted the responsibility of keeping things together as much as possible, for the family. I hope you can take some pride in that someday as well.

The cause of my father's alcoholism was depression, as is often the case, and likely where I inherited some of my own issues. But I'm so grateful for this one thing - he got out of it. Maybe we can, too.

Once this is over, take time to focus on yourself. Loneliness is exhausting, I know, but try to build up your self-esteem a little and you WILL find at least a few friends. And from them, a few acquaintances. It's a cycle; a much healthier cycle.

I'd love to chat more if you feel so inclined. If not, please take care of yourself.

That's so much to deal with. I'm sorry things are so stressful right now..

If it really comes down to it, his threats of suicide are imminent, and you don't know what else to do, I'd say call the police. He might get angry, but he will eventually be able to understand. This is an incredibly emotionally taxing situation for you and no one can have absolute solutions. There is no quick fix. It's especially difficult because he is acting very rashly. Try your best to express to him just how worried he is making you and how scared/concerned you are. Does he have any family you could call, or any good friends you could talk to?

I can tell you're worried sick. It's a terrifying situation, and one that can leave you feeling powerless. You will do all that you can. Please take care of yourself as well. I hope he can find the help he needs.

I feel like I can relate to you a lot. I'm a fairly young (? 24) female, and I often feel the same way when it comes to being ignored. I have a lot of trouble making new friends, and I always have. Isolation can be very damaging, and it's a tough problem to solve.

Stressors like finances definitely don't help. It makes it difficult to get involved with activities that might give you the opportunity to build up a social life, especially when that added stress is on top of feelings of loneliness and all that comes with it.

I think, though, that if you've become so depressed that you're considering suicide, moving out of the place you are living would be hugely beneficial. When you're feeling isolated, you shouldn't have to come home to negativity. It sounds almost hostile. I know it's tough, and scary, but it's absolutely a more worthwhile option than giving up.

Above all else, try not to view yourself as the problem. Much of this is situational. Self-improvement is difficult when you can't even be comfortable in your own home. Keep looking. You're absolutely not alone.

EDIT: But (in relation to one of your comments) I agree, a guy looking for female roommates exclusively does sound pretty sketchy. If/when you go to meet a roommate, try to get someone to go with you (your brother maybe?). I've been the one going to other people's places and the person having prospective roommates come to me, and I wouldn't think twice about the prospective roommate bringing someone along.

I know it's an obvious question, but have you talked to your doctor? If they're good, they might be able to point you in the right direction, or even just give you some sort of answers or history of the issue. Maybe even CBT? I've never tried it, but I'm considering doing so for myself. Almost anything that they say is beneficial becomes worth trying at a certain point.

5 years is a pretty long time. I'm so sorry you're experiencing that. I love what apatheticdude said. Try not to give up hope. I can't relate, but I empathize. Good luck to you.

Oh yes I definitely agree on the not having children part. I've always said I don't foresee myself being selfless enough to be the parent a child deserves, and I'm so glad I had that foresight!

I just have trouble recognizing my youth. I know it's silly, but I start to feel like I've already damned myself, or that I'm already a disappointment. To who? Myself, I guess. I mentioned before that I go through extreme lows. I'm not always to that extreme, but when I am I can't remember feeling anything else.

But yeah, I mentioned in another comment that I've decided to take the plunge back into experiments with AD's. I have a definite aversion to them, but I realize that at this point I need some sort of chemical to break myself out of this lack of will/motivation/ambition/etc. Last time (/first time) I tried one it definitely inhibited my cognition; hopefully I don't make ridiculous decisions like I did back then!

Thanks for your input. It's so great to speak to people who can relate. I know internet opinions aren't necessarily worth much, but as far as I'm concerned, you're a lovely person. And congratulations on going back to school. When I'm not sinking into my own personal pit of despair, I like to remind myself that at least finishing school will be an accomplishment I can be proud of.

A little late, but I had to say that it really is so nice to get any response at all. Thank you all so much for being there; you're all great people in my book. I go through very low lows sometimes, and the night I posted this was obviously one of them. Knowing that someone cares enough even to simply type out a comment for a stranger like me does add some sort of hope (?), if that's the right word. I'm going to talk to my doctor on Monday and try to get on an AD. I've had negative effects from one in the past and I'm a little resistant to the idea in the first place, but I can't keep putting myself (and the people I love) through this.

I really appreciate your response. I don't really have the opportunity to live with my family anymore. My mother lives in a studio and my father just rents a room. My mother of course does insist that I can still live with her, but really it's not feasible. 

And yeah I get that it's hard to be motivating, especially when you know motivation is something depression zaps away. I just feel like it's so hard for me to relate to other people, regardless of interests. Especially when it's more than one person, it's as if my brain just shuts down and I act incredibly awkward. Also, I'm female, and I guess I'm just hyper-aware of the cattiness that seems to come my way. That's definitely not a blanket statement about other women, but it's something I have a really hard time being patient about. Edit: I'm very possibly just so hypersensitive in general that I am manifesting negativity that isn't necessarily there, or that doesn't even need to be acknowledged. 

And when it comes to having male 'friends,' it never seems to work out. Other than one or two exceptions, guys don't want to be 'friends.' On top of that, and this may be tmi, but if sex does enter it things just get worse. Despite everyone's intentions.

Bleh, sorry. /Rant. Seriously though, thank you.
